title: Compute lifecycle: build the in-house gated lifecycle on the native RunPod API; do not wrap SkyPilot for RunPod now
summary: Based on EXP-0009. Wrapping SkyPilot for RunPod would (a) give no stop, only terminate, so the mandatory max-runtime auto-stop becomes auto-destroy anyway; (b) add a second lifecycle state store (~/.sky) that the write-ahead spend reservation and reconcile would have to chase; (c) require a plaintext ~/.runpod/config.toml, which conflicts with secrets:// references and the never-write-plaintext rule; (d) add a large dependency for a single provider. The in-house gated provisioning interface (compute.provision/status/stop/destroy/reconcile, budget.effective preconditions, write-ahead reservation, idempotent launch-or-lookup) owns state and secrets, and a native RunPod adapter is the next step behind it. Revisit SkyPilot (or dstack) as an optional adapter when multi-cloud placement or spot-instance recovery across providers is needed, or if RunPod stop/multi-node support lands upstream.
